text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Amid growing friction within the opposition Conservative Party, supporters of new leader Per Stig Moeller are demanding that his predecessor Hans Engell explain his lack of support for Moeller in an open fight with powerful party veteran Anne Birgitte Lundholt. The Moeller camp fears that Engell and Lundholt are conspiring to oust the new party chairman.
--Copenhagen Port Authority posted a disappointing 1996 result with operating profits down at 26 million crowns and sale of land accounting for the surplus rather than core activities.

--Malaysian Penang Shipbuilding Construction's Amin Shah, who is currently negotiating for a 48 percent shareholding in J.Lauritzen's Danyard shipyard in west Denmark, sees the yard's future as specialising in the building of high-tech vessels.

--The Danish Employers' Association is opposed to government plans for industry to make compulsory contributions for job creation schemes for the handicapped, disabled and disadvantaged. A high 72 percent of Denmark's handicapped have work, with up to 300,000 in employment.

--Danish exports are on the way up again after treading water throughout much of 1996, with Britain, Norway and Sweden showing sizeable increases but Germany, the Danes' main foreign market, flat. Thanks to an end-year rally, exports to Britain rose 14.5 percent in 1996 to 25 billion crowns.
